newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Arthur Andersen says quality listings needed in HK.
newsitem.headline: Arthur Andersen says quality listings needed in HK.

text.p: Quality listings rather than sheer numbers should be the goal of Hong Kong's initial public offer (IPO) market which will probably stay strong in 1997, audit and business advisory services group Arthur Andersen said on Thursday.
There were 49 new listings in 1996, raising HK$20.68 billion, significantly up from 26 new listings with HK$7.64 billion raised in 1995.
"More is not necessarily better," Arthur Andersen said in a statement. "Quality listings, rather than sheer numbers, should be the territory's goal."

Kennedy Liu, partner of Arthur Andersen's Enterprise Group, said greater attention must be paid to fundamental issues such as long-term business plans, realistic industry growth projections and investors perceptions that may colour or replace reality.
Of last year's new listings, six were H-shares, 10 were spinoffs and five were by way of introduction without raising funds in the market.
Arthur Andersen's latest IPO survey report suggested that about one third of the IPOs traded below issue price at the end of 1996.
"The quality of the companies listed is of utmost importance to support a healthy share price," Liu said.
Liu said the Hong Kong Stock Exchange should assess its role continually and review its listing requirements such as track record, profit requirements and prospectuses.
The Arthur Andersen report said over 60 percent of the 1996 listings had a fully-diluted price to earnings (P.E.) ratio of less than 10 and spinoffs generally attracted a higher P.E.
Liu said he expected the 1997 listings should obtain a higher P.E. of about 7.5 to 8.0 on anticipation of better quality IPOs in 1997, compared with about 7.0 for those in 1996.

Other than H-shares which generally raised over HK$200 million and spinoffs, most listings raised less than HK$200 million each and about 60 percent of the new listings were over 10 times subscribed, the report said.
Liu estimated about 30 to 40 H-share candidates were queued up for listing in Hong Kong by the end of 1998.
Liu said he expected total funds raised in 1997 to exceed the 1996 level of over HK$20 billion.
Looking ahead, continued strong and active IPO activities were expected in 1997, he said.
